sanskrit: rakṣas tu vācā saṃpūjya praśnaṃ papraccha taṃ dvijam mokṣyase brūhi me praśnaṃ kenāsmi hariṇaḥ kṛśaḥ
english: But the demon, honoring him with courteous speech, put a question to the brāhmaṇa: "You shall go free—answer me my question: by what cause am I so green and gaunt?"

sanskrit: muhūrtam atha saṃcintya brāhmaṇas tasya rakṣasaḥ ābhir gāthābhir avyagraḥ praśnaṃ pratijagāda ha
english: Then the brāhmaṇa, having reflected for a moment, calmly answered that demon's question with these verses.

sanskrit: videśastho vilokastho vinā nūnaṃ suhṛjjanaiḥ viṣayān atulān bhuṅkṣe tenāsi hariṇaḥ kṛśaḥ
english: "Living abroad, dwelling apart, surely cut off from your friends, you enjoy peerless pleasures all alone—that is why you are green and gaunt.

sanskrit: nūnaṃ mitrāṇi te rakṣaḥ sādhūpacaritāny api svadoṣād aparajyante tenāsi hariṇaḥ kṛśaḥ
english: Surely your friends, O demon, though well treated by you, are estranged through your own fault—that is why you are green and gaunt.

sanskrit: dhanaiśvaryādhikāḥ stabdhās tvadguṇaiḥ paramāvarāḥ avajānanti nūnaṃ tvāṃ tenāsi hariṇaḥ kṛśaḥ
english: Surely men richer in wealth and power, arrogant, yet in worth far beneath you, look down upon you—that is why you are green and gaunt.

sanskrit: guṇavān viguṇān anyān nūnaṃ paśyasi satkṛtān prājño 'prājñān vinītātmā tenāsi hariṇaḥ kṛśaḥ
english: Being yourself a man of merit, you surely see others without merit being honored; wise and disciplined, you see the unwise so treated—that is why you are green and gaunt.

sanskrit: avṛttyā kliśyamāno 'pi vṛttyupāyān vigarhayan māhātmyād vyathase nūnaṃ tenāsi hariṇaḥ kṛśaḥ
english: Though afflicted by lack of livelihood, you scorn the means of getting one, and out of high-mindedness you suffer—that is why you are green and gaunt.

sanskrit: saṃpīḍyātmānam āryatvāt tvayā kaś cid upaskṛtaḥ jitaṃ tvāṃ manyate sādho tenāsi hariṇaḥ kṛśaḥ
english: Out of nobility you pressed yourself hard to oblige someone, and he, good sir, thinks he has bested you—that is why you are green and gaunt.

sanskrit: kliśyamānān vimārgeṣu kāmakrodhāvṛtātmanaḥ manye nu dhyāyasi janāṃs tenāsi hariṇaḥ kṛśaḥ
english: I think you brood over people who, their hearts shrouded in lust and anger, torment themselves on wrong paths—that is why you are green and gaunt.

sanskrit: prājñaiḥ saṃbhāvito nūnaṃ naprājñair upasaṃhitaḥ hrīmān amarṣī durvṛttais tenāsi hariṇaḥ kṛśaḥ
english: Honored by the wise but not befriended by fools, you—modest yet impatient under the ill-conducted—that is why you are green and gaunt.

sanskrit: nūnaṃ mitramukhaḥ śatruḥ kaś cid āryavad ācaran vañcayitvā gatas tvāṃ vai tenāsi hariṇaḥ kṛśaḥ
english: Surely some enemy with a friend's face, behaving as a noble man would, has deceived you and gone his way—that is why you are green and gaunt.

sanskrit: prakāśārthagatir nūnaṃ rahasyakuśalaḥ kṛtī tajjñair na pūjyase nūnaṃ tenāsi hariṇaḥ kṛśaḥ
english: Open in your dealings, yet skilled in counsel and accomplished, you are surely not honored by those who should know your worth—that is why you are green and gaunt.

sanskrit: asatsv abhiniviṣṭeṣu bruvato muktasaṃśayam guṇās te na virājante tenāsi hariṇaḥ kṛśaḥ
english: When you speak your settled conviction among the wicked who are bent on their own way, your virtues do not shine—that is why you are green and gaunt.

sanskrit: dhanabuddhiśrutair hīnaḥ kevalaṃ tejasānvitaḥ mahat prārthayase nūnaṃ tenāsi hariṇaḥ kṛśaḥ
english: Lacking wealth, cleverness, and learning, possessed only of inner fire, you surely strive after some great thing—that is why you are green and gaunt.

sanskrit: tapaḥpraṇihitātmānaṃ manye tvāraṇyakāṅkṣiṇam bandhuvargo na gṛhṇāti tenāsi hariṇaḥ kṛśaḥ
english: I think your kinsfolk will not accept you, for your heart is fixed on austerity and you long for the forest—that is why you are green and gaunt.

sanskrit: nūnam arthavatāṃ madhye tava vākyam anuttamam na bhāti kāle 'bhihitaṃ tenāsi hariṇaḥ kṛśaḥ
english: Surely among men of wealth your speech, though faultless and uttered in good season, finds no luster—that is why you are green and gaunt.

sanskrit: dṛḍhapūrvaśrutaṃ mūrkhaṃ kupitaṃ hṛdayapriyam anunetuṃ na śaknoṣi tenāsi hariṇaḥ kṛśaḥ
english: A fool dear to your heart, fixed in his old beliefs and now angered, you are unable to win back—that is why you are green and gaunt.

sanskrit: nūnam āsaṃjayitvā te kṛtye kasmiṃś cid īpsite kaś cid arthayate 'tyarthaṃ tenāsi hariṇaḥ kṛśaḥ
english: Surely, having entangled you in some task he desired, someone now presses you exceedingly hard—that is why you are green and gaunt.

sanskrit: nūnaṃ tvā svaguṇāpekṣaṃ pūjayānaṃ suhṛd dhruvam mayārtha iti jānāti tenāsi hariṇaḥ kṛśaḥ
english: A friend whom you honor for his own qualities surely takes it for granted, "This man's purpose is served through me"—that is why you are green and gaunt.

sanskrit: antargatam abhiprāyaṃ na nūnaṃ lajjayecchasi vivaktuṃ prāptiśaithilyāt tenāsi hariṇaḥ kṛśaḥ
english: Surely, out of shame, you do not wish to disclose the intention hidden within you, slack as you are in pursuing gain—that is why you are green and gaunt.

sanskrit: nānābuddhirucīṃl loke manuṣyān nūnam icchasi grahītuṃ svaguṇaiḥ sarvāṃs tenāsi hariṇaḥ kṛśaḥ
english: Surely you wish to win over by your own virtues all the men of the world, with their differing minds and tastes—that is why you are green and gaunt.

sanskrit: avidvān bhīrur alpārtho vidyāvikramadānajam yaśaḥ prārthayase nūnaṃ tenāsi hariṇaḥ kṛśaḥ
english: Unlearned, timid, and poor, you yet long for the fame born of learning, valor, and giving—that is why you are green and gaunt.

sanskrit: cirābhilaṣitaṃ kiṃ cit phalam aprāptam eva te kṛtam anyair apahṛtaṃ tenāsi hariṇaḥ kṛśaḥ
english: Some fruit long desired you have not won at all; what you wrought, others have carried off—that is why you are green and gaunt.

sanskrit: nūnam ātmakṛtaṃ doṣam apaśyan kiṃ cid ātmani akāraṇe 'bhiśasto 'si tenāsi hariṇaḥ kṛśaḥ
english: Surely, seeing no fault of your own making within yourself, you have been blamed without cause—that is why you are green and gaunt.

sanskrit: suhṛdām apramattānām apramokṣyārthahānijam duḥkham arthaguṇair hīnaṃ tenāsi hariṇaḥ kṛśaḥ
english: You feel, untainted by gain or means, the grief, born of irreparable loss, of vigilant friends—that is why you are green and gaunt.

sanskrit: sādhūn gṛhasthān dṛṣṭvā ca tathāsādhūn vanecarān muktāṃś cāvasathe saktāṃs tenāsi hariṇaḥ kṛśaḥ
english: Seeing virtuous householders and unvirtuous forest-dwellers, the freed still bound to their dwelling—that is why you are green and gaunt.

sanskrit: dharmyam arthaṃ ca kāle ca deśe cābhihitaṃ vacaḥ na pratiṣṭhati te nūnaṃ tenāsi hariṇaḥ kṛśaḥ
english: A righteous and profitable word, spoken by you in the right time and place, surely takes no hold—that is why you are green and gaunt.

sanskrit: dattān akuśalair arthān manīṣī saṃjijīviṣuḥ prāpya vartayase nūnaṃ tenāsi hariṇaḥ kṛśaḥ
english: Wise yet wishing to live, you surely subsist on wealth given by the inept—that is why you are green and gaunt.

sanskrit: pāpān vivardhato dṛṣṭvā kalyāṇāṃś cāvasīdataḥ dhruvaṃ mṛgayase yogyaṃ tenāsi hariṇaḥ kṛśaḥ
english: Seeing the wicked flourish and the good sink down, you surely search for what is fitting—that is why you are green and gaunt.

sanskrit: parasparaviruddhānāṃ priyaṃ nūnaṃ cikīrṣasi suhṛdām avirodhena tenāsi hariṇaḥ kṛśaḥ
english: Surely you wish to do good to friends who are at odds with one another, yet without setting them against each other—that is why you are green and gaunt.

sanskrit: śrotriyāṃś ca vikarmasthān prājñāṃś cāpy ajitendriyān manye 'nudhyāyasi janāṃs tenāsi hariṇaḥ kṛśaḥ
english: I think you brood over people—learned men engaged in wrongful acts, and wise men who have not conquered their senses—that is why you are green and gaunt."

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃpūjitaṃ rakṣo vipraṃ taṃ pratyapūjayat sakhāyam akaroc cainaṃ saṃyojyārthair mumoca ha
english: The demon, thus honored, honored that brāhmaṇa in return; he made him his friend, and, having endowed him with wealth, set him free.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca pitāmaha mahāprājña sarvaśāstraviśārada āgamair bahubhiḥ sphīto bhavān naḥ prathitaḥ kule
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: O grandfather, greatly wise, versed in all the scriptures, abounding in many traditions, you are renowned in our line.

sanskrit: tvatto dharmārthasaṃyuktam āyatyāṃ ca sukhodayam āścaryabhūtaṃ lokasya śrotum icchāmy ariṃdama
english: From you, O tamer of foes, I wish to hear what is joined with dharma and artha, bringing happiness in time to come, and a wonder to the world.

sanskrit: ayaṃ ca kālaḥ saṃprāpto durlabhajñātibāndhavaḥ śāstā ca na hi naḥ kaś cit tvām ṛte bharatarṣabha
english: This time has come upon us when kinsmen and friends are hard to keep, and there is no teacher for us but you, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: yadi te 'ham anugrāhyo bhrātṛbhiḥ sahito 'nagha vaktum arhasi naḥ praśnaṃ yat tvāṃ pṛcchāmi pārthiva
english: If I, together with my brothers, am worthy of your grace, O sinless one, then deign, O king, to answer us the question that I ask you.

sanskrit: ayaṃ nārāyaṇaḥ śrīmān sarvapārthivasaṃmataḥ bhavantaṃ bahumānena praśrayeṇa ca sevate
english: This glorious Nārāyaṇa, honored by all kings, waits upon you with great regard and with reverence.

sanskrit: asya caiva samakṣaṃ tvaṃ pārthivānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ bhrātṝṇāṃ ca priyārthaṃ me snehād bhāṣitum arhasi
english: In his presence, and before all the kings and my brothers, you should, out of affection, speak for my pleasure.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā snehād āgatasaṃbhramaḥ bhīṣmo bhāgīrathīputra idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard that speech of his, Bhīṣma, son of Bhāgīrathī, moved with affection and eager joy, spoke these words.

sanskrit: hanta te kathayiṣyāmi kathām atimanoramām asya viṣṇoḥ purā rājan prabhāvo 'yaṃ mayā śrutaḥ
english: "Come now, I shall tell you a most delightful tale; long ago, O king, I heard of this power of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: yaś ca govṛṣabhāṅkasya prabhāvas taṃ ca me śṛṇu rudrāṇyāḥ saṃśayo yaś ca daṃpatyos taṃ ca me śṛṇu
english: Hear from me too the power of the god marked with the bull, and hear from me the doubt of Rudrāṇī, the doubt that arose between that divine pair.

sanskrit: vrataṃ cacāra dharmātmā kṛṣṇo dvādaśavārṣikam dīkṣitaṃ cāgatau draṣṭum ubhau nāradaparvatau
english: The righteous Kṛṣṇa undertook a vow of twelve years, and the two seers Nārada and Parvata came to behold him at his consecration.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇadvaipāyanaś caiva dhaumyaś ca japatāṃ varaḥ devalaḥ kāśyapaś caiva hastikāśyapa eva ca
english: And Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana too, and Dhaumya, best of those who murmur prayers, and Devala, and Kāśyapa, and Hastikāśyapa as well,

sanskrit: apare ṛṣayaḥ santo dīkṣādamasamanvitāḥ śiṣyair anugatāḥ sarve devakalpais tapodhanaiḥ
english: and other holy sages, endowed with consecration and self-restraint, all followed by their pupils, ascetics rich in penance, godlike.

sanskrit: teṣām atithisatkāram arcanīyaṃ kulocitam devakītanayaḥ prīto devakalpam akalpayat
english: For them the son of Devakī, well pleased, prepared a godlike welcome, the worshipful honoring of guests befitting his line.

sanskrit: hariteṣu suvarṇeṣu barhiṣkeṣu naveṣu ca upopaviviśuḥ prītā viṣṭareṣu maharṣayaḥ
english: Upon fresh green seats of gold strewn with kuśa grass the great seers, well pleased, took their places.

sanskrit: kathāś cakrus tatas te tu madhurā dharmasaṃhitāḥ rājarṣīṇāṃ surāṇāṃ ca ye vasanti tapodhanāḥ
english: Then those ascetics who dwell apart, rich in penance, made sweet discourses bound up with dharma, concerning royal sages and the gods.

sanskrit: tato nārāyaṇaṃ tejo vratacaryendhanotthitam vaktrān niḥsṛtya kṛṣṇasya vahnir adbhutakarmaṇaḥ
english: Then the divine energy of Nārāyaṇa, kindled as fuel by the practice of his vow, issued forth as fire from the mouth of Kṛṣṇa of wondrous deeds.

sanskrit: so 'gnir dadāha taṃ śailaṃ sadrumaṃ salatākṣupam sapakṣimṛgasaṃghātaṃ saśvāpadasarīsṛpam
english: That fire burned up the mountain with its trees, its creepers and shrubs, with its throngs of birds and beasts, with its predators and creeping things,

sanskrit: mṛgaiś ca vividhākārair hāhābhūtam acetanam śikharaṃ tasya śailasya mathitaṃ dīptadarśanam
english: and with deer of many shapes; the peak of that mountain, churned and blazing to behold, was rendered senseless, filled with cries of woe.

sanskrit: sa tu vahnir mahājvālo dagdhvā sarvam aśeṣataḥ viṣṇoḥ samīpam āgamya pādau śiṣyavad aspṛśat
english: But that great-flamed fire, having burned everything utterly, came near to Viṣṇu and touched his feet like a pupil.

sanskrit: tato viṣṇur vanaṃ dṛṣṭvā nirdagdham arikarśanaḥ saumyair dṛṣṭinipātais tat punaḥ prakṛtim ānayat
english: Then Viṣṇu, scourge of foes, seeing the forest burned away, by gentle castings of his gaze restored it to its natural state.

sanskrit: tathaiva sa girir bhūyaḥ prapuṣpitalatādrumaḥ sapakṣigaṇasaṃghuṣṭaḥ saśvāpadasarīsṛpaḥ
english: And so that mountain once more had its creepers and trees in full flower, resounding with flocks of birds, with predators and creeping things.

sanskrit: tad adbhutam acintyaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā munigaṇas tadā vismito hṛṣṭalomā ca babhūvāsrāvilekṣaṇaḥ
english: Seeing that wonder, beyond thought, the company of sages then became amazed, their hair bristling and their eyes wet with tears.

sanskrit: tato nārāyaṇo dṛṣṭvā tān ṛṣīn vismayānvitān praśritaṃ madhuraṃ snigdhaṃ papraccha vadatāṃ varaḥ
english: Then Nārāyaṇa, best of speakers, seeing those seers filled with amazement, asked them modestly, sweetly, and tenderly:

sanskrit: kim asya ṛṣipūgasya tyaktasaṅgasya nityaśaḥ nirmamasyāgamavato vismayaḥ samupāgataḥ
english: "Why has amazement come upon this throng of seers, who have forever renounced attachment, who are free of 'mine' and versed in sacred lore?

sanskrit: etaṃ me saṃśayaṃ sarvaṃ yāthātathyam aninditāḥ ṛṣayo vaktum arhanti niścitārthaṃ tapodhanāḥ
english: This whole doubt of mine the blameless seers, rich in penance, ought to resolve for me truly and with certainty."

sanskrit: ṛṣaya ūcuḥ bhavān visṛjate lokān bhavān saṃharate punaḥ bhavāñ śītaṃ bhavān uṣṇaṃ bhavān eva pravarṣati
english: The seers said: "You send forth the worlds, and you withdraw them again; you are the cold, you are the heat, and it is you yourself who send down the rain.

sanskrit: pṛthivyāṃ yāni bhūtāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca teṣāṃ pitā tvaṃ mātā ca prabhuḥ prabhava eva ca
english: Of all beings upon the earth, the unmoving and the moving, you are the father and the mother, the lord, and the very source.

sanskrit: etan no vismayakaraṃ praśaṃsa madhusūdana tvam evārhasi kalyāṇa vaktuṃ vahner vinirgamam
english: Explain to us this thing that fills us with wonder, O slayer of Madhu; you alone, O blessed one, are fit to tell of the issuing-forth of that fire.

sanskrit: tato vigatasaṃtrāsā vayam apy arikarśana yac chrutaṃ yac ca dṛṣṭaṃ nas tat pravakṣyāmahe hare
english: Then we too, our terror gone, O scourge of foes, O Hari, shall tell you what we have heard and what we have seen."

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca etat tad vaiṣṇavaṃ tejo mama vaktrād viniḥsṛtam kṛṣṇavartmā yugāntābho yenāyaṃ mathito giriḥ
english: Vāsudeva said: "This is that Vaiṣṇava energy that issued from my mouth—the dark-tracked fire, bright as the world's end, by which this mountain was churned.

sanskrit: ṛṣayaś cārtim āpannā jitakrodhā jitendriyāḥ bhavanto vyathitāś cāsan devakalpās tapodhanāḥ
english: And you seers, who have conquered anger and subdued your senses, godlike, rich in penance, fell into distress and were shaken.

sanskrit: vratacaryāparītasya tapasvivratasevayā mama vahniḥ samudbhūto na vai vyathitum arhatha
english: From me, wholly absorbed in the practice of my vow through the keeping of ascetic observances, this fire arose; you should not be troubled at all.

sanskrit: vrataṃ cartum ihāyātas tv ahaṃ girim imaṃ śubham putraṃ cātmasamaṃ vīrye tapasā sraṣṭum āgataḥ
english: I have come to this fair mountain to perform my vow, and I have come to bring forth by penance a son equal to myself in valor.

sanskrit: tato mamātmā yo dehe so 'gnir bhūtvā viniḥsṛtaḥ gataś ca varadaṃ draṣṭuṃ sarvalokapitāmaham
english: Then my own self that dwells in this body, becoming fire, issued forth and went to behold the boon-giving grandfather of all the worlds.

sanskrit: tena cātmānuśiṣṭo me putratve munisattamāḥ tejaso 'rdhena putras te bhaviteti vṛṣadhvajaḥ
english: And by him, O best of sages, I was instructed regarding sonship: the bull-bannered god said, 'A son shall be yours from half of this energy.'

sanskrit: so 'yaṃ vahnir upāgamya pādamūle mamāntikam śiṣyavat paricaryātha śāntaḥ prakṛtim āgataḥ
english: That fire, drawing near to me, to the soles of my feet, attended me like a pupil and then, grown calm, returned to its natural state.

sanskrit: etad asya rahasyaṃ vaḥ padmanābhasya dhīmataḥ mayā premṇā samākhyātaṃ na bhīḥ kāryā tapodhanāḥ
english: This secret of the wise lotus-naveled one I have told you out of love; let no fear be felt, O you rich in penance.

sanskrit: sarvatra gatir avyagrā bhavatāṃ dīrghadarśanāḥ tapasvivratasaṃdīptā jñānavijñānaśobhitāḥ
english: Yours is an untroubled passage everywhere, O far-seeing ones, blazing with ascetic vows, resplendent with knowledge and discernment.

sanskrit: yac chrutaṃ yac ca vo dṛṣṭaṃ divi vā yadi vā bhuvi āścaryaṃ paramaṃ kiṃ cit tad bhavanto bruvantu me
english: Whatever you have heard or seen, in heaven or upon earth, that is some surpassing wonder—that, I pray, you tell to me.

sanskrit: tasyāmṛtanikāśasya vāṅmadhor asti me spṛhā bhavadbhiḥ kathitasyeha tapovananivāsibhiḥ
english: I have a longing for that honeyed speech, like nectar, spoken here by you who dwell in the penance-grove."

sanskrit: yady apy aham adṛṣṭaṃ vā divyam adbhutadarśanam divi vā bhuvi vā kiṃ cit paśyāmy amaladarśanāḥ
english: "Even though I, O you of stainless vision, may see something divine and wondrous to behold, unseen before, whether in heaven or on earth,

sanskrit: prakṛtiḥ sā mama parā na kva cit pratihanyate na cātmagatam aiśvaryam āścaryaṃ pratibhāti me
english: that supreme nature of mine is nowhere thwarted, and the sovereign power that abides within myself appears no wonder to me.

sanskrit: śraddheyaḥ kathito hy arthaḥ sajjanaśravaṇaṃ gataḥ ciraṃ tiṣṭhati medinyāṃ śaile lekhyam ivārpitam
english: For a matter that is credible, once told and reaching the ears of the good, abides long upon the earth, like a writing graven on rock.

sanskrit: tad ahaṃ sajjanamukhān niḥsṛtaṃ tatsamāgame kathayiṣyāmy aharahar buddhidīpakaraṃ nṛṇām
english: Therefore, in that gathering, I shall day after day repeat what has come from the mouths of the good, which kindles the understanding of men."

sanskrit: tato munigaṇāḥ sarve praśritāḥ kṛṣṇasaṃnidhau netraiḥ padmadalaprakhyair apaśyanta janārdanam
english: Then all the throngs of sages, reverent in the presence of Kṛṣṇa, gazed upon Janārdana with eyes like lotus petals.

sanskrit: vardhayantas tathaivānye pūjayantas tathāpare vāgbhir ṛgbhūṣitārthābhiḥ stuvanto madhusūdanam
english: Some, in like manner, exalted him; others honored him; and they praised the slayer of Madhu with words whose meanings were adorned with verses of the Ṛg.

sanskrit: tato munigaṇāḥ sarve nāradaṃ devadarśanam tadā niyojayām āsur vacane vākyakovidam
english: Then all the throngs of sages appointed to the discourse Nārada, who beholds the gods and is skilled in speech.

sanskrit: yad āścaryam acintyaṃ ca girau himavati prabho anubhūtaṃ munigaṇais tīrthayātrāparāyaṇaiḥ
english: "That wonder, beyond thought, O lord, which was experienced upon the Himālaya mountain by the throngs of sages intent on pilgrimage to the holy fords—
